answer: Run a reef census crew: each new account joins a survey team on one reef transect anchored at a relic wreck marker. Weekly the crew counts fish along it and submits the tally plus a photo of the marker. Counts are checked against two independent crews on the same reef; a crew whose numbers diverge beyond tolerance loses its stake and its sponsor's bond. A yarrow sprig planted at the shore station each season is a living timestamp: crews photograph its growth beside the marker, so old photos cannot be reused. A Sybil farm would need real divers at reefs weekly, not just fresh accounts.
